_about: Applicant-facing wording (Decisions 30, 31, 33). Single source of truth for the API (serving/app.py), the dashboard (dashboard/scoring.py) and the public site (website/public/assets/reasons.js). The applicant sees an outcome (approved, or needs a manual review; never declined), the details of their own that counted, details to check, and model-tested changes. Model issues and the review cutoff are never shown to the applicant; they are in the risk officer output.

approved.headline: Your application has been approved
approved.summary: The details you gave allowed an automatic approval.
approved.why_intro: What counted most in your favour:
approved.why_none: Your details were close to those of a typical applicant.
next_steps: Your repayments will follow the plan you chose.
This is a demonstration on synthetic data. It is not financial advice.

manual_review.headline: Your application needs a manual review
manual_review.summary: We could not make an automatic decision, so a risk officer will review your application before a final decision is made. It has not been declined.
manual_review.why_intro: What counted against an automatic approval:
manual_review.why_none: No single detail stood out. A risk officer will look at the application as a whole.
next_steps: A risk officer will review your application and the details you gave.
If any detail is wrong, ask for it to be corrected before the review.
This is a demonstration on synthetic data. It is not financial advice.

check.intro: Please check these details are correct:

issues.out_of_range: {label} of {value} is outside the range we can assess automatically
issues.thin_long_history: your credit file is marked as limited, but shows {months} of credit history
issues.thin_many_accounts: your credit file is marked as limited, but shows {accounts}
issues.full_short_history: your credit file is marked as full, but shows only {months} of credit history
issues.full_no_accounts: your credit file is marked as full, but shows {accounts}
issues.commitments_vs_income: your existing commitments of {obligations} a month are high against an income of {income}

changes.order_value_gbp: Apply for a smaller amount: an order of {value} instead of {current}.
changes.n_instalments: Choose a plan of {value} instead of {current}.
changes.existing_monthly_obligations_gbp: Reduce your existing monthly commitments to {value} (currently {current}).

changes_text.intro: Each of these on its own, with everything else the same, would have led to an automatic approval:
changes_text.none: No single change to the order, the repayment plan, your existing commitments or your savings would be enough on its own. A risk officer will look at the application as a whole.
changes_text.note: These changes do not guarantee approval. A future application will be assessed on your circumstances at that time.

method.new: Each detail was compared with a typical applicant by changing that one detail and re-scoring with the model.
method.existing: Each detail was compared with a typical customer by changing that one detail and re-scoring with the model.

error_labels.missing_information: Known blind spot (information the model lacks)

data_input.name: Inputs consistent with the training data
data_input.ok: All inputs inside the training ranges and consistent with each other.

missing_information.name: Known blind spot: full credit file
missing_information.triggered: Full credit file, score at or above the group's {pct}th-percentile line ({line}).
missing_information.ok: Full credit file, score below the group's {pct}th-percentile line ({line}).

overreliance.name: Recommendation rests on one detail
overreliance.triggered: {name}: setting it alone to typical would change the recommendation, and it carries most of the total effect.
overreliance.ok: No single detail decides the recommendation.

officer.divergence_note: The model's score is below the review threshold, but a check requires a person: the applicant is told the application needs a manual review.

record.approver_note: Not recorded: the approval gate does not capture approver identity (Decision 23).
lineage: Decision 27: champion {model_version}, promoted on validity grounds
Decision 27: business cutoff {cutoff}, PD at or above it refers for review
Decision 30: plain-English reasons, one input at a time against a typical applicant
Decision 31: error-type checks and risk officer flag (rules {rules_version})
Decision 33: applicant outcome (approved or manual review), own-detail reasons, model-tested changes

data.method: These figures count the {n} past customers in the model's training data, in groups of at least {min_group}. They describe what happened to similar customers, not what will happen to you.
